paper_metadata.title: Attention Is All You Need
paper_metadata.primary_contribution: Introduces the Transformer: a sequence transduction architecture that removes recurrence and convolution, using only (multi-head) self-attention and feed-forward layers within an encoder–decoder framework.

prerequisites.name: Encoder–Decoder Sequence-to-Sequence Models
prerequisites.description: A family of models where an encoder converts an input sequence into a continuous representation and a decoder autoregressively generates an output sequence conditioned on that representation.
prerequisites.why_needed: The Transformer retains the encoder–decoder paradigm but replaces the recurrent/convolutional cores with attention-only blocks.

prerequisites.name: RNN/LSTM/GRU and Their Sequential Limitations
prerequisites.description: Recurrent networks process tokens sequentially, building hidden states that depend on previous steps. This limits parallelism and increases the number of sequential operations as sequence length grows.
prerequisites.why_needed: Motivates removing recurrence to enable parallel training and shorter path lengths for long-range dependencies.

prerequisites.name: Convolutional Seq2Seq Models (ByteNet/ConvS2S/Extended Neural GPU)
prerequisites.description: CNN-based transduction models parallelize across positions but require paths that grow with distance (linear or logarithmic) to connect distant tokens.
prerequisites.why_needed: Provides the efficiency/expressivity contrast the Transformer improves upon by making path length constant via attention.

prerequisites.name: Attention Mechanisms
prerequisites.description: Compute weighted combinations of value vectors using compatibility between a query and keys. Allow models to focus on relevant parts of sequences irrespective of distance.
prerequisites.why_needed: The Transformer is built entirely from attention, replacing recurrence/convolution for dependency modeling.

prerequisites.name: Self-Attention (Intra-Attention)
prerequisites.description: An attention pattern where queries, keys, and values come from the same sequence, enabling each position to attend to all other positions to build contextualized representations.
prerequisites.why_needed: Core mechanism inside both Transformer encoder and decoder to compute contextual features.

prerequisites.name: Encoding Positional Information
prerequisites.description: Because attention layers are permutation-invariant, explicit position signals (learned or fixed) are required to inject order into token representations.
prerequisites.why_needed: Transformer uses sinusoidal positional encodings summed with token embeddings to convey order without recurrence.

prerequisites.name: Residual Connections and Layer Normalization
prerequisites.description: Residual connections add sub-layer inputs to outputs, and LayerNorm stabilizes activations. Together they enable deep stacking and stable optimization.
prerequisites.why_needed: Wrapped around each attention and feed-forward sub-layer in the Transformer for trainability.

prerequisites.name: Autoregressive Decoding and Causal Masking
prerequisites.description: Decoders generate tokens left-to-right, conditioning on past outputs only. Causal masks prevent access to future positions during training and inference.
prerequisites.why_needed: Explains why the Transformer decoder uses masked self-attention and shifted targets.

high_level_components.name: Encoder Token + Positional Embedding
high_level_components.description: Converts input tokens to continuous vectors and injects order information by summing sinusoidal positional encodings. Produces the initial sequence of embeddings used by the encoder stack.
high_level_components.purpose: Provide content and position-aware representations to an attention-only encoder.

high_level_components.name: Transformer Encoder Stack (N layers)
high_level_components.description: A stack of identical layers, each combining multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network, with residual connections and LayerNorm. Encodes the input sequence into contextual representations.
high_level_components.purpose: Model global dependencies among input tokens in parallel and produce a memory for the decoder.

high_level_components.name: Encoder Multi-Head Self-Attention
high_level_components.description: Applies several attention heads in parallel over the encoder inputs, each attending to different relational subspaces and positions. Outputs are concatenated and projected to mix head information.
high_level_components.purpose: Capture diverse relationships and long-range dependencies efficiently within the input sequence.
high_level_components.input: Embeddings or previous encoder layer outputs (as Q=K=V)

high_level_components.name: Position-wise Feed-Forward Network
high_level_components.description: Applies the same two-layer MLP with nonlinearity to each position independently. Acts as a content-wise transformation following attention mixing.
high_level_components.purpose: Introduce nonlinearity and per-token transformation after attention.
key_properties: shared across positions within a layer

visual_reference.location_in_figure: blocks labeled 'Feed Forward' in both stacks

high_level_components.name: Residual Add & LayerNorm Wrapper
high_level_components.description: Wraps each sub-layer (attention or feed-forward) with a residual connection followed by layer normalization. Ensures stable training of deep stacks.
high_level_components.purpose: Stabilize gradients and ease optimization while enabling deep stacking.

high_level_components.name: Decoder Token + Positional Embedding (shifted)
high_level_components.description: Embeds the previously generated output tokens (shifted right) and adds positional encodings. Forms the decoder’s input at each time step during training and inference.
high_level_components.purpose: Provide ordered representations of prior outputs for autoregressive decoding.

high_level_components.name: Transformer Decoder Stack (N layers)
high_level_components.description: A stack of identical layers combining masked multi-head self-attention, encoder–decoder attention, and a position-wise feed-forward network, each wrapped by Add & Norm. Produces contextualized decoder states for next-token prediction.
high_level_components.purpose: Generate outputs autoregressively while conditioning on both past outputs and the encoded input.
high_level_components.input: Position-enriched decoder embeddings and encoder memory

high_level_components.name: Decoder Masked Multi-Head Self-Attention
high_level_components.description: Multi-head self-attention applied to decoder inputs with a causal mask that blocks access to future positions. Maintains the autoregressive property.
high_level_components.purpose: Ensure each prediction depends only on earlier outputs while modeling intra-target dependencies.
high_level_components.input: Decoder embeddings or previous decoder layer outputs

visual_reference.location_in_figure: right stack block labeled 'Masked Multi-Head Attention'

high_level_components.name: Encoder–Decoder Multi-Head Attention
high_level_components.description: Decoder queries attend over the encoder’s memory (keys/values), enabling the decoder to condition its predictions on the entire input sequence.
high_level_components.purpose: Fuse source-side information into the decoder at every layer.
high_level_components.input: Queries from decoder; keys/values from encoder outputs

visual_reference.location_in_figure: middle block in right stack labeled 'Multi-Head Attention' with arrow from encoder

high_level_components.name: Multi-Head Attention
high_level_components.description: Projects queries, keys, and values into multiple subspaces, applies scaled dot-product attention in parallel across heads, concatenates the results, and applies a final projection.
high_level_components.purpose: Allow the model to attend to different types of relationships simultaneously while keeping computation efficient.
key_properties: efficient compared to single high-dim head

high_level_components.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
high_level_components.description: Computes attention weights via scaled dot-products between queries and keys, applies optional masking, softmax, and weighted sum over values.
high_level_components.purpose: Core attention operation used within each head for stability and efficiency.

high_level_components.name: Output Projection and Softmax
high_level_components.description: Maps decoder states to vocabulary logits via a linear layer followed by softmax to produce next-token probabilities. Weights are tied with embeddings in the original design.
high_level_components.purpose: Produce a probability distribution over the next output symbol.

high_level_relationships.description: Position-enriched input embeddings are fed into the encoder stack for contextualization via attention and feed-forward sub-layers.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: Token indices → dense embeddings with positions → contextual encoder representations

high_level_relationships.description: Each encoder layer contains a multi-head self-attention sub-layer.
Each encoder layer applies a position-wise feed-forward network after attention.
Residual connections and LayerNorm wrap both sub-layers within each encoder layer.
Multi-head attention is realized by running several scaled dot-product attentions in parallel and combining their outputs.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: Q,K,V → per-head outputs → concatenated and projected output

high_level_relationships.description: Encoder self-attention uses the multi-head attention mechanism with Q=K=V from the encoder layer inputs.
Shifted decoder embeddings with positions are fed into the decoder stack to produce states for next-token prediction.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: Previous outputs → embeddings with positions → decoder states

high_level_relationships.description: Each decoder layer begins with masked multi-head self-attention.
Each decoder layer includes encoder–decoder attention where decoder queries attend to encoder memory.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: Decoder features + encoder memory → cross-attended features

high_level_relationships.description: A position-wise feed-forward network follows the attention blocks in each decoder layer.
The encoder’s final representations serve as keys and values for encoder–decoder attention.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: Encoder memory → conditioning signals for the decoder

high_level_relationships.description: Final decoder states are projected to vocabulary logits and normalized to probabilities.
During autoregressive generation, the selected next token is shifted and re-embedded as input to the decoder for the subsequent step.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: Predicted token → discrete id → embedding with position

high_level_relationships.description: General attention concept underpins the specific scaled dot-product formulation used throughout the model.
Self-attention concept explains why Q, K, V originate from the same sequence in encoder layers.
Autoregressive decoding necessitates masking future positions in the decoder’s self-attention.
Need for order information motivates adding positional encodings to token embeddings on the encoder side.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: No order signal → embeddings with absolute/relative position cues

high_level_relationships.description: Decoder inputs also require positional information to maintain order during generation.
The attention-only encoder replaces recurrent layers, removing the sequential computation bottleneck.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: Sequential hidden-state updates → fully parallel attention-based encoding

high_level_relationships.description: Compared to CNN-based transduction models, the Transformer encoder achieves constant path length between tokens via self-attention.
high_level_relationships.data_transformation: Distance-dependent convolutional paths → direct attention links

main_pipeline.name: Input Representation
main_pipeline.description: Map input tokens to embeddings and add positional encodings.

main_pipeline.name: Source Encoding
main_pipeline.description: Process the sequence in parallel through stacked self-attention and feed-forward layers to form encoder memory.

main_pipeline.name: Decoder Input Preparation
main_pipeline.description: Shift previous outputs, embed them, and add positions; apply masked self-attention.

main_pipeline.name: Cross-Attention with Encoder Memory
main_pipeline.description: Allow decoder queries to attend to all encoder positions to fuse source information.

main_pipeline.name: Decoder Transformation and Output Projection
main_pipeline.description: Apply position-wise feed-forward and output projection to produce next-token probabilities.

main_pipeline.name: Autoregressive Feedback
main_pipeline.description: Sample or select the next token and feed it back for the next decoding step.

parallel_pathways.description: Attention is computed across multiple heads in parallel, each focusing on different subspaces/relations.
Each sub-layer output is combined with its input through residual addition followed by normalization.

feedback_loops.description: Autoregressive decoding loop where generated tokens are shifted and re-fed into the decoder.

key_innovations.name: Attention-Only Encoder–Decoder (No Recurrence/Convolution)
key_innovations.description: Replaces RNN/CNN cores with stacks of self-attention and feed-forward layers. This removes sequential dependencies within training examples and shortens the path length between any two positions to constant.
key_innovations.comparison_to_baseline: RNNs require sequential steps; CNNs need multiple layers to connect distant tokens. Transformer processes all positions in parallel via attention.
key_innovations.expected_benefit: Significantly increased parallelism and better long-range dependency modeling, yielding stronger accuracy with lower training cost.

key_innovations.name: Multi-Head Attention
key_innovations.description: Introduces multiple attention heads operating on projected subspaces and aggregates them. This counters the averaging effect of single-head attention and allows modeling of diverse relations concurrently.
key_innovations.comparison_to_baseline: Single-head attention mixes all relations into one space; multi-head attends to multiple subspaces in parallel.
key_innovations.expected_benefit: Improved expressivity without large computational overhead.

key_innovations.name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
key_innovations.description: Uses dot-product compatibility with 1/sqrt(dk) scaling to prevent softmax saturation and supports efficient batched matrix multiplications.
key_innovations.comparison_to_baseline: Compared to additive attention, this is faster and more memory-efficient; compared to unscaled dot-product, it stabilizes gradients for large dk.
key_innovations.expected_benefit: Stable and efficient attention computation enabling deep, wide models.

key_innovations.name: Sinusoidal Positional Encodings
key_innovations.description: Adds fixed sinusoidal signals to token embeddings to encode positions without recurrence. The design supports learning relative position-dependent attention and can extrapolate to longer sequences.
key_innovations.comparison_to_baseline: Replaces learned or recurrent position handling with a simple, fixed signal summed with embeddings.
key_innovations.expected_benefit: Provides order information while maintaining simplicity and potential length generalization.

design_decisions.decision: Wrap every attention and feed-forward sub-layer with residual addition followed by LayerNorm.
design_decisions.rationale: Stabilizes optimization and enables deeper stacks of layers.

design_decisions.decision: Use causal masking in decoder self-attention with shifted-right targets.
design_decisions.rationale: Preserves the autoregressive property by blocking future information during training and inference.

design_decisions.decision: Share weights between token embeddings and the output projection.
design_decisions.rationale: Reduces parameters and can improve consistency between input and output spaces.

design_decisions.decision: Adopt fixed sinusoidal positional encodings rather than learned ones.
design_decisions.rationale: Comparable performance with potential extrapolation to longer sequences and no extra parameters.

design_decisions.decision: Use multi-head attention with reduced per-head dimensions.
design_decisions.rationale: Maintains computational cost similar to single-head attention while improving expressivity.

high_level_summary.one_sentence_summary: The Transformer performs sequence transduction using an attention-only encoder–decoder with multi-head self- and cross-attention, positional encodings, and autoregressive decoding.
high_level_summary.paragraph_summary: Inputs are embedded and enriched with positional encodings, then processed in parallel by a stack of encoder layers built from multi-head self-attention and position-wise feed-forward networks. The decoder consumes shifted output embeddings, applies masked multi-head self-attention to maintain causality, and attends to the encoder’s memory via cross-attention. After another feed-forward transformation, a linear–softmax layer produces next-token probabilities, which feed back into the decoder during generation. The architecture removes recurrence/convolution, enabling high parallelism and strong long-range dependency modeling.
high_level_summary.conceptual_analogy: Like a committee of experts (heads) each reading the entire document and then pooling their insights, rather than a single person reading word-by-word sequentially.
high_level_summary.key_insight: Global self-attention can replace recurrence and convolution entirely—yielding constant path length between tokens and full parallelism—when combined with multi-head diversity, residual normalization, and explicit positional information.
